summary: This Dockerfile creates a Ubuntu container with Zsh shell, Oh-My-Zsh framework, and syntax highlighting plugin. It customizes the shell prompt to visually indicate you're running inside a container, then sets Zsh as the default command when the container starts.

explanations.3: This tells the Ubuntu package installer to not prompt for user input during setup, which is necessary in Docker since there's no interactive terminal to respond to prompts.
explanations.6: The --no-install-recommends flag tells the package manager to skip optional packages that normally come along with these tools, keeping the final image smaller.
explanations.11: After installing packages, this deletes the apt cache files that are no longer needed, reducing the image size.
explanations.14: This downloads and runs the Oh-My-Zsh installer script directly from GitHub; the curl flags make it fail on errors and run silently.
explanations.15: The --unattended flag runs the installer without prompts, and --keep-zshrc preserves any existing Zsh configuration instead of replacing it.
explanations.18: The --depth=1 flag tells git to only download the latest commit history instead of the full history, making the clone much faster and smaller.
explanations.20: This uses sed to find the line that starts with 'plugins=(git)' and replace it to add zsh-syntax-highlighting to the list of active plugins.
explanations.25: The -i flag makes Zsh interactive and -l makes it a login shell, so it reads your configuration files when starting.
